articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License for International Development Bank for Investment and Finance
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Iran General License FF-1, titled "Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance."

This amended general license supersedes and replaces the previous General License FF. It specifically authorizes the wind-down of transactions involving the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance, also known as Iraq Development Bank, and certain majority-owned entities through December 1, 2026.
The new license mandates that any payments to blocked persons must be made into blocked accounts, ensuring compliance with existing sanctions regulations during the wind-down period.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities for North Korea IT Worker Schemes and DRC Destabilization
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in North Korean government-run IT worker schemes and those supporting destabilizing activities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Specifically, OFAC sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in North Korean IT worker schemes that defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for the DPRK's weapons programs. These schemes often involve fraudulent identities and deceptive tactics to secure employment.

Additionally, OFAC sanctioned the Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Zigama Credit and Savings Society, a Rwandan financial institution, for facilitating Rwanda's support for the M23 movement and its political wing in eastern DRC.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a $1,529,685 settlement with Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-headquartered cloud networking solutions provider.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks exported networking equipment and related services on nine occasions from the United States to Joint Stock Company (JSC) Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer. MMZA was blocked by operation of law due to its majority ownership by the designated entity JSC Concern Almaz Antey, even though MMZA itself was not directly listed on the SDN List until June 2022.

OFAC determined that these apparent violations were voluntarily self-disclosed and egregious. The settlement amount reflects a reduction from the statutory maximum due to the voluntary self-disclosure, despite findings of reckless disregard for U.S. sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Frequently Asked Questions on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has amended 11 of its Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.

These revisions are part of an ongoing review to ensure that OFAC's published guidance remains current. The updated FAQs clarify when financial institutions must freeze funds due to a blocked person's interest versus rejecting a prohibited transaction where no blockable interest exists.

The amendments also address reporting procedures, including the 10-business-day deadline for reporting blocked property and rejected transactions, required supporting documentation, and annual reporting requirements for blocked property.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related and Russia-Related General Licenses, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses, alongside the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea.

Specifically, OFAC issued Iran General License GG, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving Karnakis and Karnakis, and Iran General License HH, authorizing wind-down activities, limited safety and environmental transactions, and the offloading of cargo involving certain persons or vessels blocked on October 21, 2026.
The action also included the issuance of amended Frequently Asked Questions to provide further guidance on these changes.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements PAIPA Designations and Issues Associated General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) and issued associated General Licenses.

OFAC issued PAIPA General License 1, "Transactions Authorized Pursuant to the Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations," and PAIPA General License 2, "Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving Certain Entities Blocked on October 19, 2026."

Additionally, OFAC added several entities to its Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions List (NS-MBS List), including Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase I Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership, Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase II Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership, and Qiji Chuangtan Beijing Investment Management Co Ltd, all based in China.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / U.S. Department of State

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License for Earthquake Relief
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Venezuela-related General License 60A, titled "Authorizing Transactions Related to Earthquake Relief Efforts in Venezuela."

This amended general license replaces and supersedes previous authorizations for earthquake relief. OFAC also issued one amended Frequently Asked Question, FAQ 1263, to provide further clarity on the scope of authorized activities.
This action reflects OFAC's continued efforts to facilitate humanitarian aid to Venezuela while maintaining its sanctions program.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related and Cuba Entities, Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related and Cuba designations, alongside the issuance of new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions.
Among the actions, the Department of State designated Cuba's BANCO INTERNACIONAL DE COMERCIO S.A. (BICSA) pursuant to E.O. 14404, for providing services to designated Iran entities.

OFAC also issued an Iran-related general license covering the wind-down of transactions involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance, and two Russia-related general licenses authorizing certain transactions involving Lukoil retail service stations outside Russia and certain Lukoil entities in Bulgaria.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / U.S. Department of State

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuelan National Assembly President Jorge Rodriguez Gomez from SDN List
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has removed Jorge Jesus Rodriguez Gomez, President of Venezuela's National Assembly, from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List.
Rodriguez Gomez, who was initially designated in 2018, is no longer subject to asset freezes and other restrictions for U.S. persons.

This delisting signals a strategic shift in U.S. policy towards Venezuela, moving from punitive economic containment to structured engagement with the Venezuelan regime, and is seen as part of a broader three-phase plan for Venezuelan stabilization.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities in Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Actions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations under its Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism sanctions programs.

These actions target individuals and entities involved in illicit drug trafficking and terrorism financing networks. The designations include individuals linked to the Cartel del Noreste (CDN) and its financial networks.

The Treasury Department highlighted its ongoing efforts to disrupt the financial infrastructure of transnational criminal organizations and terrorist groups that pose a threat to U.S. national security.

Zelenskyy warned that the US was distracted by its midterm elections, while local authorities in the Kharkiv region reported at least 62 people wounded in a combined missile and drone attack that damaged a medical facility and residential buildings.

articles.headline: UN General Assembly and Security Council to Elect Five International Court of Justice Judges
body: The United Nations General Assembly and Security Council will meet concurrently today to fill five vacancies on the International Court of Justice (ICJ), the principal judicial organ of the United Nations.
Based in The Hague, the ICJ comprises 15 judges serving nine-year terms, with five seats coming up for election every three years. No two judges may be nationals of the same State.

Candidates must secure an absolute majority in both the 193-member Assembly and the 15-member Council, which vote independently by secret ballot. The veto does not apply, and multiple rounds of voting may be necessary.
articles.source: UN Meetings Coverage and Press Releases

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
